title: Winter surface density leads sigma0 26.5 oxygen by 1 yr at BATS (r 0.82) but explains only part of the loss size; CMIP6 ssp585 ends the open North Pacific 26.5 outcrop by 2027-2068
abstract: Question: does the loss of the winter outcrop of sigma0 26.5 explain the size of the oxygen (O2) loss on this surface in the North Pacific (NP) and at BATS, and what do CMIP6 projections imply? Approach: we built public outcrop indices for 1950-2026 from ERSSTv5 SST and WOA23 decadal salinity, tested lagged O2 links with phase-surrogates, scaled the year-to-year O2-index slope by the epoch change of the index, and added CMIP6 (6 models, ssp585) winter density changes to the observed field. Results: the NP area with winter sigma0 >= 26.5 fell from 0.94 (1984-1996) to 0.36 million km2 (2009-2025); WOA23 decades give 1.14 (1985-1994) to 0.14 (2015-2022). BATS O2 on 26.5 followed winter sigma0 of the Eighteen Degree Water formation box (30-40 N, 75-45 W) at a 1-yr lag (detrended r 0.82, p < 0.001), as did the 26.5 class thickness (r 0.78). In the NP the pre-specified public replication passed in 1 of 3 regions (170-180 E: r 0.59, p < 0.001). The year-to-year slope predicted 0.27 (0.09-0.66) of the BATS loss with the full index and 0.83 (0.35-1.76) with SST only; in the NP the ratios were 0.15-1.26 with wide intervals and near 0 with an unsmoothed index. Models made the observed NP surface lightening (-0.03 to -0.19 vs -0.14 kg/m3), but the two largest changes were in models with no 26.5 outcrop. Under ssp585 the NP area >= 26.5 fell below 10% of 1984-1996 in 2027-2068 and was near zero in all models by 2081-2100. Interpretation: the outcrop link is real and fast, but under a linear fast-response model it explains only part of the loss; slower ventilation memory or higher O2 use at fixed age must supply the rest. Limitations: no interannual salinity in the index; the NA size result depends on the salinity treatment; sparse NP ship series; one member per model; surface density is a proxy for subduction.
